transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I suppose what finally scared me into coming in today is... after I eat too much, I’ve been making myself throw up in the bathroom. I do it so I won’t gain weight. I kept telling myself it was just a one-time mistake, but it's gotten to the point where it isn't just a mistake anymore. It keeps happening, and I knew I needed to talk to someone about it.

When you say you eat too much before making yourself throw up, can you describe what a typical episode looks like—how much food are you eating, and do you feel like you can't control or stop the eating once it starts?

Well, it usually happens when I'm alone. Like, after a bridge night, or if I've worked a late shift at the store. I might come home and just... eat. I'll go through leftover casserole, some cookies I baked, crackers, and ice cream, all in one sitting. It's a lot. I mean, it's much more than I’d ever put on a plate in front of anyone. 

And to answer your other question, yes. Once I start eating like that, it really does feel like I can't stop myself. I just keep going until I've had all of it.
How often have these binge-eating and vomiting episodes been occurring, and for how many months has this pattern been going on?

Well, for at least the past several months... it's been happening most weeks. I'll have one of those secret eating spells and then go make myself sick afterward. I guess I can't honestly call it occasional anymore. It's pretty much a weekly thing now.
Would you say your sense of self-worth or how you feel about yourself is strongly tied to your weight or body shape?

Yes, I'd say it is. Honestly, if my skirt feels tight before church, or if I catch my side view in the store mirror at work, it can ruin my whole day. I just feel like everyone can tell I've let myself go, and it really gets to me. It's hard to feel good about anything else when I'm feeling that way about my body.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, or if you know it, your body mass index?

I'm about five foot four. As for my weight, I'm... I'm really not sure right now. I try not to step on the scale too often because it just upsets me. And I don't know my body mass index, I've never really kept track of that number.

Even without a scale, do you have a sense of whether you're currently underweight, at a normal weight, or overweight for your height, and has your weight changed noticeably over the past several months?

Well, I'd say I'm probably around a normal weight, maybe a little on the heavier side, but definitely not underweight. My clothes still fit mostly the same, so I don't think my weight has changed all that much over the last few months. It just... fluctuates a little bit here and there.
